title: I should have taken the direct flight
goal: Evaluate a past travel decision and choose a practical next step
freeConversationInstruction: Talk about decisions you would make differently and discuss what you learned from them

pages.title: Review the last lesson
pages.instruction: Recall how earlier events explain a later problem

items.prompt: What had happened before someone arrived late?
How did that affect the next event?
What could they check before a future trip?

pages.title: Name the pictures
pages.instruction: Say each word or expression in English, then click a picture to check and listen

items.audioText: a direct flight. The direct flight cost more.
a connecting flight. We missed the connecting flight.
a delay. There was a fifty-minute delay.
a boarding gate. Check the boarding gate again.

items.example: A refund has not been confirmed
items.audioText: a refund. A refund has not been confirmed.

items.example: We need to check the travel insurance

pages.title: Read the situation
pages.instruction: Read for the facts and the different priorities
pages.author: Scenario briefing · fictional
pages.subject: I should have taken the direct flight
paragraphs: Travel record: planned connection, 35 minutes. First flight delayed, 50 minutes. A more expensive direct flight had been available when booking. No replacement, refund or insurance decision has yet been confirmed. Explain the timing before judging the choice.

pages.title: Practise the conversation
pages.instruction: You are Ana and Teacher is Kim. Practise together, swap roles, then answer the questions

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: Did you make the connection? You only had thirty-five minutes
lines.audioText: Did you make the connection? You only had thirty-five minutes.
lines.translation: Você conseguiu pegar a conexão? Só tinha trinta e cinco minutos

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: No. The first flight was fifty minutes late, so I missed it
lines.audioText: No. The first flight was fifty minutes late, so I missed it.
lines.translation: Não. O primeiro voo atrasou cinquenta minutos, então perdi a conexão

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: That’s frustrating. Was there a direct flight when you booked?
lines.audioText: That’s frustrating. Was there a direct flight when you booked?
lines.translation: Que frustrante. Havia voo direto quando você reservou?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Yes, but it cost more. I should have allowed more time between flights
lines.audioText: Yes, but it cost more. I should have allowed more time between flights.
lines.translation: Sim, mas custava mais. Eu deveria ter deixado mais tempo entre os voos

questions.hint: The delay was …, but the connection was …
questions.answer: The first flight was fifty minutes late, but the connection allowed only thirty-five minutes

questions.prompt: Was a direct flight available when booking?
questions.answer: Yes, a direct flight was available but it cost more

questions.prompt: What does Ana think she should have allowed?
questions.answer: Ana thinks she should have allowed more time between flights

pages.title: Practise the conversation
pages.instruction: You are Ana and Teacher is Kim. Practise together, swap roles, then answer the questions

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: You couldn’t have known about the delay, though. What can you do now?
lines.audioText: You couldn’t have known about the delay, though. What can you do now?
lines.translation: Mas você não tinha como saber do atraso. O que pode fazer agora?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: I’m waiting for the desk to confirm another flight
lines.audioText: I’m waiting for the desk to confirm another flight.
lines.translation: Estou esperando o atendimento confirmar outro voo

lines.speaker: Kim
lines.text: I’d also check what your travel insurance covers, without assuming it pays for everything
lines.audioText: I’d also check what your travel insurance covers, without assuming it pays for everything.
lines.translation: Eu também conferiria o que o seguro cobre, sem presumir que paga tudo

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: I will. Next time I’d compare the arrival time as well as the price
lines.audioText: I will. Next time I’d compare the arrival time as well as the price.
lines.translation: Vou conferir. Da próxima vez compararia o horário de chegada e também o preço

questions.prompt: What is Ana waiting for now?
questions.answer: Ana is waiting for the desk to confirm another flight

questions.prompt: What does Kim suggest checking about insurance?
questions.answer: Kim suggests checking what the insurance covers without assuming it covers everything

questions.prompt: What will Ana compare next time besides price?
questions.answer: Ana will compare the arrival time as well as the price

pages.title: Look back at the journey
pages.instruction: Compare the connection time with the flight delay. Discuss other booking choices with Teacher

pages.title: Look back with should have and could have
pages.instruction: Use a modal plus have plus a past participle to evaluate past choices

rows.subject: A better past choice
rows.example: I should have allowed more connection time

rows.subject: A choice to avoid
rows.example: I shouldn’t have booked such a short connection

rows.subject: A past alternative
rows.example: I could have booked the direct flight, but I didn’t

pages.note: These examples look back at decisions that cannot now be changed. Use the past participle after have: taken, chosen, booked. Could have can have other meanings in other contexts.

pages.title: Use the information to respond
pages.instruction: A better travel plan. Explain what went wrong and suggest a better choice

pages.title: Listen and answer
pages.instruction: An option is still possible. Listen for the new information and decide how to respond
pages.message: Hi, Ana. There’s still a flight available this evening. It leaves at six and gets in at eight thirty, but the desk hasn’t confirmed a seat yet. The direct flight tomorrow morning would arrive at ten and costs more. The traveller needs to be there by nine tomorrow, so the evening option could work if a seat is confirmed. Could you explain the two choices and what must be checked? A refund and insurance payment have not been confirmed
pages.audioText: Hi, Ana. There’s still a flight available this evening. It leaves at six and gets in at eight thirty, but the desk hasn’t confirmed a seat yet. The direct flight tomorrow morning would arrive at ten and costs more. The traveller needs to be there by nine tomorrow, so the evening option could work if a seat is confirmed. Could you explain the two choices and what must be checked? A refund and insurance payment have not been confirmed.
pages.greeting: There’s still a flight we could ask about

items.prompt: When would the evening flight arrive?
items.answer: The evening flight would arrive at eight thirty that night

items.prompt: Why would tomorrow’s direct flight not meet the deadline?
items.answer: It arrives at ten, after the traveller’s nine o’clock deadline

items.prompt: What must be confirmed before choosing the evening option?
items.answer: The desk must confirm a seat on the evening flight

pages.title: Respond to the message
pages.instruction: Recommend a next step, with a condition. Use the message to update your response and agree on the next step

pages.title: Before booking the trip
pages.instruction: Watch the travel decision and its consequence, then suggest a better plan

items.prompt: Where did the traveller choose to go, and why?
items.hint: Listen for the country and the place he wanted to visit
items.answer: He chose a small French town because he had heard about its art gallery

items.prompt: What happened when he asked for directions?
items.hint: Did anyone manage to help him?
items.answer: He asked for directions, but nobody could help him

items.prompt: How did the journey affect his visit to the gallery?
items.hint: Separate the difficult journey from the quality of the gallery
items.answer: The journey was so long and difficult that he did not enjoy the gallery when he finally arrived. He does not say that the gallery itself was bad

items.prompt: What should he have checked, and what would you do next time?
items.hint: Use should have or could have, then suggest a practical next step
items.answer: Example: He should have checked how to get to the gallery and how long the journey would take. Next time, I would plan the route before booking and save clear directions
